The '''2016 [[Tippeligaen]]''' was the 72nd completed season of top-tier [[Association football|football]] in [[Norway]]. The competition began on 11 March 2016. Due to the [[UEFA Euro 2016|2016 UEFA European Championship]], there was a break between the rounds played on 29 May and 3 July. The decisive matches of the home-and-away season were played on 6 November 2016. A promotion/relegation play-off between the third-from-bottom team of the Tippeligaen and the winner of the promotion play-offs of the [[2016 1. divisjon]] was contested on 30 November and 4 December 2016.<ref name=matchdates>{{cite web|title=Hovedterminliste menn 2016|trans-title=Main schedule men's football 2016|url=http://www.fotball.no/Documents/Bilder/NFF/2015/NFF-nyheter/hovedterminliste%20menn%202016%20oppdatert.pdf|website=fotball.no|publisher=[[Football Association of Norway]]|access-date=26 November 2015}}</ref>

The league was contested by 16 teams: the 13 best teams of the 2015 season; the two teams who won direct promotion from the [[2015 1. divisjon]], [[Sogndal Fotball|Sogndal]] and [[SK Brann|Brann]]; and [[IK Start|Start]], who won the promotion/relegation play-off finals against [[FK Jerv|Jerv]].

The 2016 season was the last season the league was named ''Tippeligaen''. The league changed its name to ''Eliteserien'' ahead of the [[2017 Eliteserien|2017 season]], a non-sponsor affiliated name controlled by the [[Football Association of Norway]].

==Teams==
Sixteen teams competed in the league – the top fourteen teams from the previous season, and two teams promoted from [[2018 1. divisjon|1. divisjon]].

==Relegation play-offs==
{{Main|2016 Eliteserien promotion/relegation play-offs}}
The 14th-placed team, [[Stabæk Fotball|Stabæk]], took part in a two-legged play-off against [[FK Jerv|Jerv]], the winners of the 2016 1. divisjon [[2016 1. divisjon#Promotion play-offs|promotion play-offs]], to decide who would play in the [[2017 Eliteserien]].
{{football box
|date       = {{Start date|2016|11|30|df=y}}

|score      = 1–0

|goals2     =

|attendance = 1,750 
|referee    = Dag Roger Nebben
}}
{{football box
|date       = {{Start date|2016|12|4|df=y}}

|team1      = [[Stabæk Fotball|Stabæk]]
|score      = 2–0

}}
''Stabæk won 2–1 on aggregate and retained their place in the [[2017 Eliteserien]]; Jerv remained in the [[2017 1. divisjon|1. divisjon]].''
